FN-U967LXG-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 287
Committee: County and Municipal Sponsor: Representative Juandalynn Givan
Government
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/17/2025
House Bill 287 as introduced could increase the administrative obligations of the county and
municipal law enforcement agencies to report the number of sworn law enforcement officers
employed by each agency. This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of the
Alabama State Law Enforcement Agency to adopt rules to implement these provisions.

FN-U967LXG-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 287
Committee: County and Municipal Sponsor: Representative Juandalynn Givan
Government
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/19/2025
House Bill 287 as reported by the Committee on County and Municipal Government could
increase the administrative obligations of a state, county, or municipal law enforcement agency
to report the number of sworn law enforcement officers employed by each agency. This bill
would also increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama State Law Enforcement
Agency to adopt rules to implement these provisions.
Additionally, this bill could reduce funding to any state, county, or municipal agency by an
undetermined amount dependent on the amount of grant funding administered by the Alabama
Department of Economic and Community Affairs that is withheld for failure to submit the
reports required by the provisions of this bill.

FN-U967LXG-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 287
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Representative Juandalynn Givan
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 03/18/2025
House Bill 287 as passed the House of Representatives could increase the administrative
obligations of a state, county, or municipal law enforcement agency to report the number of
sworn law enforcement officers employed by each agency. This bill would also increase the
administrative obligations of the Alabama Justice Information Commission to adopt rules to
implement the provisions of this bill.
Additionally, this bill would increase receipts to the State General Fund and increase the
financial obligations of any state, county, or municipal law enforcement agency, that fails to
submit reports required pursuant to the provisions of this bill, from the assessment of a $1,000
fine, and an additional $1,000 fine every 30 days until the law enforcement agency is in
compliance.
Finally, this bill could reduce funding to any state, county, or municipal agency by an
undetermined amount dependent on the amount of any state grant funding that is withheld for
failure to submit the reports required by the provisions of this bill.
